analysis.title: One horseman short of an apocalypse
key_insights: Brent has risen roughly $10 in a month as Middle East tensions return. Rumours of planned US/Israeli strikes on Iran and reports of further ships damaged in the Strait of Hormuz are putting the geopolitical risk premium back into oil.
European natural gas and electricity prices are also climbing again, so the oil move could become a broader energy-driven inflation problem.
French 10-year spreads versus Germany have widened about 50bp in a month. The report frames this as shifting from a French political problem to a European bond-market problem.
French spreads are approaching levels previously associated with major episodes of European financial stress, and spreads across Europe's periphery are also widening.
French equities have had their worst relative performance in three decades. The CAC is at a record low relative to the broader European market (source: Morgan Stanley chart).
Nvidia's five-year CDS has widened about 35bp in a month. CDS spreads are widening across the hyperscaler universe, with some names at levels associated with significant credit risk.

Credit concern centers on circular financing in the AI ecosystem. Suppliers, hyperscalers and AI labs increasingly fund one another, and vendor-financing announcements have risen sharply (SEB X-Asset, TS Lombard charts).
Hyperscaler earnings expectations have barely changed since July despite the AI boom, meaning no corresponding upward revisions (Marquee chart).
Weakness has spread from hyperscalers to semiconductor stocks. Semiconductors now trade at a forward P/E discount to the S&P 500, so some bad news is priced in (Koyfin chart).
Market bubbles have historically peaked around 40% concentration, and the AI Big 10 are in that neighborhood. Railroads reached 63% as the exception (Flow Show chart).
The SOX is tracking a pattern similar to the dot-com bubble, when new supply arrived as demand began to fade (SEB X-Asset chart).
The report summarizes three risks: oil threatens inflation, France threatens European bonds, and AI threatens the market's most crowded growth narrative.

sector_views.rationale: Semis have weakened after hyperscalers lost momentum, but trade at a forward P/E discount to the S&P 500, so some bad news is priced in. The report asks whether this is a rotation or something worse.

earnings_insights: Hyperscaler earnings expectations have barely moved since July, with no upward revisions despite continued AI enthusiasm (Marquee chart).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Geopolitical risk premium is returning to oil, which the report says is a threat to a fragile global economy and to inflation.
Spreads are approaching levels tied to past episodes of European financial stress, with spillover to peripheral spreads.

macro_indicators.indicator: European natural gas and electricity prices
macro_indicators.interpretation: Energy costs are widening the oil move into a broader inflation risk.

risk_factors: Oil and energy shock feeding inflation, with Brent up about $10 in a month and European gas and power prices rising.
French political risk spreading into European bond markets and peripheral spreads.
AI credit stress from circular financing and widening CDS, with end-user demand not yet catching up.
Flat hyperscaler earnings revisions despite elevated AI expectations.
AI concentration near historical bubble levels and a SOX pattern resembling the dot-com period.
